ledger.claim: This trip runs on an UPFRONT_QUOTE fare: EV-FARE-00115 records fare_model UPFRONT_QUOTE, quoted_fare_sgd of 34.50 carried on the base_fare line, and total_charged of 39.00 with refund_issued_sgd of 0.00. The rider was therefore made to pay 4.50 more than the quote she was shown, which is the opposite of the driver's statement that 'the fare was fixed anyway, she paid the quote'. Under POL-RD-11 the live question on an upfront trip is precisely what was charged on top of the quote, and every figure in the remedy is derived from these two numbers.

The AYE (Alexandra Rd towards Tuas) gantry line of 2.00 is a phantom charge. The erp_gantry_proximity block derived from EV-GPS-00115 places the trace's closest approach to that gantry at 5,419.29 m - some 5.4 km - and that nearest fix is index 0, the very first fix of a 100%-coverage trace, so the vehicle was nowhere near the AYE at any point in the trip; the gantry is also flagged on_optimal_route false, the optimal route being KPE then CTE then SLE. Under POL-RD-09(4) a line for a gantry the trace never passes is a billing-integrity failure, refunded in full as a standalone correction, available whether or not a deviation exists, and it is recorded as a billing-integrity finding in the ruling's referrals. POL-RD-10(8) is not engaged, because a line refunded under POL-RD-09(4) is its express carve-out.

The amount properly refundable to this rider is 2.00, and the ledger's own arithmetic says so. Charged_total is 39.00; quoted_fare_sgd is 34.50; the only properly chargeable pass-through lines are the KPE (Defu Flyover towards ECP) gantry at 2.50, which the trace passes within 44.50 m while on the optimal route and which the rider does not dispute, together with an airport surcharge of 0.00 and a waiting_time_fee of 0.00. POL-RD-11(a) refunds the excess in full, and EV-FARE-00115's derived pol_rd_11_remedy publishes exactly that figure, 2.00, rounded up to the nearest 0.05 as the fare_model requires.

The detour itself is established on this trip's own trace: EV-GPS-00115 records 28.18 km driven against EV-TRIP-00115's 22.40 km platform optimal, an excess of 5.78 km and 25.8%, past both POL-RD-01 establishment tests of 0.8 km and 20%, and POL-RD-01 makes the trace figure, not the rounded trip_record copy, the governing one. That excess is what put the vehicle on the KPE/TPE corridor and it is why the trace never comes near the AYE. The rider's advocate does not press the distance element separately, because on an upfront-quoted fare POL-RD-11 fixes the distance and time lines at booking and closes the POL-RD-02 route however large the excess; the deviation is relied on here as the factual foundation for the phantom-gantry correction, not as a second head of refund.

The driver's external-cause excuse must be discarded. His explanation for leaving the optimal corridor - 'CTE northbound was heavy', repeated in the 21:14:10 chat message 'CTE very heavy boss, i go KPE then TPE' - is tested under POL-RD-13 against the traffic_advisory for this trip and nothing else. The bundle holds no such advisory: EV-ADVIS-00115-01 is MISSING, carries weight 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, and has no payload, so the comparison POL-RD-03 requires cannot be run, POL-RD-03 is unavailable, and the assertion carries no weight under POL-RD-08.

This case must be decided with money moving, not escalated. The driver cited no advisory evidence ID for his traffic excuse, so the absent advisory is not an exculpatory clause invoked against a cited artifact within POL-RD-10(5): POL-RD-13(1) provides that an assertion citing no artifact cannot be invoked against one, and that an absent artifact no party has cited is a gap in the bundle rather than a contradiction in it. Nor does POL-RD-10(3) apply, because the trace is not impaired, and POL-RD-10(8) is answered by the POL-RD-09(4) carve-out for the phantom AYE line. Escalation would be terminal and would replace the 2.00 correction the rider is owed with a held amount. (EV-ADVIS-00115-01 is the MISSING advisory, weight 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT.)

POL-RD-04 does not exonerate any part of the excess, as the admissibility note on EV-CHAT-00115 itself records. The only message from the rider in the chat log is MSG-00115-002, the single word 'ok', sent at 21:14:50 in reply to the driver's own announcement that he was diverting; it comes after the decision, it names no road or place, and its waypoint_hint is null, so it is neither a rider instruction nor corroborable by any route the trace shows the vehicle travelling. The rider acknowledged a diversion she was told about; she did not request it.

The trace is clean for policy purposes, so the excess stands at the measured figure and no gap-handling discount applies. EV-GPS-00115 carries 229 fixes at a 10.0 second sample interval with 100.0% coverage, a max_gap_sec of 0.0 and an empty gaps array, none of which meets the POL-RD-07(a)-(c) thresholds of a gap over 90 seconds, a jump over 500 m or a sustained interval over 30 seconds; the admissibility pre-pass confirms COMPLETE at weight 1.0. The deviation is therefore established on the trace alone and needs no corroboration beyond it.

No additional corroboration burden falls on this rider. EV-RPROF-00115 shows deviation_claims_60d of 0 and deviation_claims_60d_substantiated of 0, so the POL-RD-08 condition that would require corroboration beyond the gps_trace for an excess below 30% is not met, and the rider's claim stands on the artifacts already cited.

EV-FARE-00115 records fare_model UPFRONT_QUOTE with quoted_fare_sgd 34.50, so this trip's distance and time charges were fixed at booking and POL-RD-11 bars any distance-or-time refund however large the excess; the rider's request to be refunded the 'extra distance' must be refused outright, because the detour cost her nothing on those lines.

The bill reconciles to the cent: the 34.50 quoted fare plus 4.50 of ERP equals the 39.00 charged, so the whole of the excess over the quote is the two ERP lines and not one cent of it is distance or time. Under POL-RD-11(a) the rider's recovery is 39.00 less 34.50 less the 2.50 properly chargeable KPE toll, i.e. 2.00, and the POL-RD-11(b) pass-through correction is not added on top of that figure.

The KPE (Defu Flyover towards ECP) charge of 2.50 is properly chargeable under POL-RD-09: that gantry lies on the optimal route and the trace's nearest fix passes 44.5 m from it, far inside the 250 m match radius, so the rider did cross it and none of that 2.50 is refundable.

The AYE (Alexandra Rd towards Tuas) line is not on the optimal route and the trace's closest approach to that gantry is 5,419 m, more than twenty times the 250 m crossing radius, so it was never crossed; on this record it supports no more than a standalone billing-integrity correction of 2.00 under POL-RD-09(4), which POL-RD-09(1) forbids counting twice and POL-RD-11(b) forbids stacking on any distance refund. That 2.00, not 6.00, is the ceiling on this claim.

The trace is unimpaired for policy purposes: 229 fixes at a 10 s interval, 100% coverage, no gaps and a maximum gap of 0 s, so POL-RD-07's gap limbs are not engaged and it is the trace figure of 28.18 km, not the rounded trip_record convenience copy, that POL-RD-01 measures against the 22.4 km optimal.

Even taken at its highest the deviation is not material: the excess is 5.78 km and 25.80% of the 22.4 km optimal, above the POL-RD-01 establishment gate of 0.8 km and 20% but below the 50% and 8.0 km material gate, so POL-RD-06's uplift to FULL_REFUND and its driver-conduct referral are not engaged and the rider's remedy stays confined to the pass-through lines.

Even if POL-RD-06 were consulted on the profile, the driver records deviation_flags_90d of 1 against completed_trips_90d of 523 — a rate of 0.19%, against thresholds of 3 flags or 5% — so no repeat-deviation pattern is established and no uplift or referral can rest on this driver's record.

The driver's account of CTE congestion is tested under POL-RD-13 against the traffic advisory for this trip and nothing else: EV-ADVIS-00115-01 is MISSING with weight 0.0 and issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT — an impairment I disclose — so under POL-RD-08 the assertion carries no weight and supplies no amended optimal. Because no advisory identifier is cited as an exculpatory clause, POL-RD-13(1) applies and this is not a POL-RD-10(5) escalation: the case should be decided on the money, capped at the 2.00 pass-through correction.

ruling.explanation:
To both parties: this trip ran on an upfront quote, and that is what controls the money.

The deviation is real. EV-GPS-00115 records 28.18 km driven against the 22.40 km platform optimal on EV-TRIP-00115 — an excess of 5.78 km and 25.8%, past both POL-RD-01 gates of 0.8 km and 20%. POL-RD-01 makes the trace figure, not the rounded trip_record copy, the governing one. But EV-FARE-00115 shows fare_model UPFRONT_QUOTE with quoted_fare_sgd 34.50, so under POL-RD-11 the distance and time charges were fixed at booking, the detour cost the rider nothing on those lines, and no distance refund is available however large the excess. The request to be refunded the 'extra distance' is refused on that ground; POL-RD-02 does not run.

What is refundable is the billing. The rider was quoted 34.50 and charged 39.00. Two ERP lines make up the 4.50 difference. The KPE (Defu Flyover towards ECP) line of 2.50 lies on the optimal route and the trace passes within 44.5 m of it — a crossing, well inside the 250 m match radius — so it is properly chargeable and stands. The AYE (Alexandra Rd towards Tuas) line of 2.00 is phantom: it is not on the optimal route, and the trace's closest approach to it is 5,419 m (at index 0, the first fix of a 100%-coverage trace). Under POL-RD-09(4) that line is refunded in full as a standalone billing-integrity correction. POL-RD-11(a) therefore gives 39.00 charged, less 34.50 quoted, less 2.50 properly chargeable (airport surcharge 0.00, waiting fee 0.00) = 2.00. POL-RD-11(b) is not added on top of (a): the same 2.00 is already excluded from the properly chargeable lines, so counting it again would refund it twice. Amount refunded: 2.00, rounded up to the nearest SGD 0.05.

The driver's account — 'CTE northbound was heavy', repeated in chat MSG-00115-001 at 21:14:10 — is tested under POL-RD-13 against this trip's traffic advisory and nothing else. EV-ADVIS-00115-01 is MISSING, weight 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, so the POL-RD-03 comparison cannot be run, POL-RD-03 is unavailable, and the assertion carries no weight under POL-RD-08 and supplies no amended optimal. It changes no money here because the upfront fare fixes the distance line regardless. POL-RD-04 gives the driver nothing either: the rider's only message is 'ok' at 21:14:50 — an acknowledgement of a diversion she was told about, not an instruction, naming no road or place, with waypoint_hint null.

No escalation. The trace is unimpaired under POL-RD-07(a)–(c) (229 fixes, 10 s interval, 100% coverage, max gap 0 s), so no independent-corroboration question arises. No party cited the advisory as an exculpatory clause, so the absent advisory is a gap in the bundle rather than a POL-RD-10(5) contradiction (POL-RD-13(1)). The unmatched AYE line is refunded under POL-RD-09(4), which POL-RD-10(8) expressly carves out. And the deviation is not material (25.8% and 5.78 km, below the 50% and 8.0 km gates), so POL-RD-06 is not engaged; in any event the driver's profile shows deviation_flags_90d of 1 against 523 completed trips in 90 days, far below the 3-flag or 5% pattern thresholds, so it supports no uplift and no conduct referral.

No driver compensation is due: nothing on this upfront trip was billed by distance, so there is no unbilled-kilometre shortfall.

This ruling rests on EV-FARE-00115 and EV-GPS-00115, both weight 1.0, so confidence is set at 0.90.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
referrals: POL-RD-09(4) billing integrity — the AYE (Alexandra Rd towards Tuas) gantry line of SGD 2.00 on EV-FARE-00115 was charged although the GPS trace EV-GPS-00115 never came within 5,419 m of that gantry and the gantry is not on the optimal route. Refund it as a standalone pass-through correction and log this phantom charge line for billing-integrity review.
